clue.text: Cheating at cards, using duplicity?

definitions.meaning: deceitful behaviour, playing a two-faced game
read literally, dealing a doubled hand of cards, duplicity as twofold dealing

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: dealing with duplicity taken as dealing everything twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicitous conduct in business or friendship is the established idiom for two-faced cheating.

clue.text: Topical changes of view

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word before it are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A newsy subject keeps shifting the way people see it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sight or vision is what the adjective means, so it stands for of view.

clue.text: The end of spinnaker in large sailing ship

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for large

parts.note: large means big

indicators.note: The end of picks out only the final letter of the sail's name that follows

explanation.surface: The tip of a big sail on a tall ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of' gives R, the last letter of spinnaker, and 'in' places it inside BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted, square-rigged vessel is the specific type of sailing ship named.

clue.text: Junior officers, they climb the mast

definitions.meaning: the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy, once also in the British army
flags hoisted up a flagpole or mast

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both low-ranking officers and the flags they once carried, which are run up masts.

clue.text: It's glee, strangely, shown by a mournful poet

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the words alongside are jumbled into an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Joy appears oddly in the work of a gloomy versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges ITS and GLEE together; the irony is that glee is what a writer of laments lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of elegies, mournful poems for the dead, is a mournful poet by trade.

clue.text: Piece of meat lion chewed up

indicators.note: chewed up suggests the word is mangled, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A big cat has torn into a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut from the back of an animal between ribs and hips is a common piece of meat.

clue.text: Will it cause bankruptcy in the fishing industry?

definitions.text: Will it cause bankruptcy in the fishing industry?

parts.words: Will it cause bankruptcy in the fishing industry?
parts.note: the accounting term for a deficit after all costs, read as the loss of fishing nets

explanation.definitionFit: An overall deficit after expenses is what drives a firm to bankruptcy, and fishermen use nets.

clue.text: Risk total defeat at Wimbledon, perhaps

definitions.text: Risk total defeat at Wimbledon, perhaps

parts.words: Risk total defeat at Wimbledon, perhaps
parts.note: the idiom for inviting ruin, read as a catastrophe on a tennis court; Wimbledon is the famous London tennis tournament

explanation.definitionFit: To invite catastrophe is the idiom; on a tennis court a calamity is literally on court.

clue.text: Communication from a solicitor?

parts.note: a solicitor here is someone who solicits, asking for money, not the British lawyer

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a solicitor is a kind of lawyer, which is the false lead; here it is one who solicits donations.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal for money sent by post is the written message someone asking for funds sends.

clue.text: New ones may be expensive if stout, perhaps

definitions.text: New ones may be expensive if stout, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words beside it could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A larger person may pay more for fresh clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IF and STOUT; the whole clue also describes the answer, since bigger sizes can cost more.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets of clothes are things a stout person might find dearer to buy new.

clue.text: Letter or note to devout holy man found by the French

parts.note: E is a musical note
pi is informal for pious or devout
ST is the abbreviation for saint
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone writes a note to a pious French saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter, such as those of the apostles in the New Testament.

clue.text: Stand torture

definitions.meaning: a framework for holding things, such as a wine or plate stand
to torment, as on the medieval stretching frame

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a holding frame and the act of inflicting severe pain.

clue.text: Turkish leader elected for a second time

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish commander or chief
a successful candidate is in

explanation.surface: A Turkish chief wins office once more.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a title for an Ottoman officer, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more, a second time, is exactly what the adverb means.

clue.text: Far-reaching hunger

definitions.meaning: to yearn or crave, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective of great extent and a verb meaning to yearn.

clue.text: Cancel space flight, there's an unpleasant smell in craft

indicators.note: in tells us the smell goes inside the word for craft

parts.note: craft means skill or art
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Mission control scraps a launch because the capsule stinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off a mission before completion is the standard space-flight term.

clue.text: Sailors take a turn round these parts — about time

definitions.text: Sailors take a turn round these

indicators.note: about tells us the word for parts goes around the letter for time

parts.note: parts means bits

explanation.surface: Seamen wind their rope around fittings in this area, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like part of 'these parts' meaning this area; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Posts on a ship's deck around which cables are wound are what sailors loop lines round.

clue.text: Edibles put out for French music master

indicators.note: put out suggests the word is disturbed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food is laid out for a French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges EDIBLES. Léo Delibes was a 19th-century French composer of Coppélia.
explanation.definitionFit: Delibes was a French composer, so a master of music from France.

clue.text: Attempts to sell a dummy — touchdowns possible

definitions.meaning: to try it on is to attempt a deception, as in selling a dummy in rugby
in rugby a try is a touchdown, and if tries are on they are possible

explanation.walkthrough: Selling a dummy is a rugby feint, faking a pass; a try is rugby's touchdown score.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying it on means attempting a deceit; and tries being on means scoring is possible.

clue.text: Where those about town come from?

definitions.text: Where those about town come from?

parts.words: Where those about town come from?
parts.note: man-about-town people, read as those living around the town, on its outskirts

explanation.definitionFit: Residential outskirts surround a town, so people round about it live there.

clue.text: Some terrible mishap results in a scar

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nasty accident leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark or flaw on the skin; the verb form means to spoil or mar, as a scar does.

clue.text: Stout aunt's off to church

indicators.note: off suggests the word is spoilt, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is kept here as a letter

explanation.surface: A plump aunt heads off to Sunday worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges AUNTS into STAUN. 'Stout' here means steadfast, not plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout in the sense of loyal and firm, like a stout supporter, is a synonym.

clue.text: Tom's shout showing disapproval

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a shout is a call

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom yells his disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a tomcat's yowl is the jeering whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or jeer from an audience expresses disapproval.

clue.text: Exclusive group with resting place up country

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A clique has a bed set up in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small select circle of people sharing interests is what the noun means.

clue.text: Bill includes broken chair that's antique

indicators.note: includes tells us the account word holds the jumbled furniture inside it

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the next word are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: An invoice lists a damaged old chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' and 'includes' look like a damaged item being listed; AC (account) is the usual crossword shorthand for a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Very old or old-fashioned, belonging to a past era, matches antique.

clue.text: Outhouse made redundant

definitions.meaning: a small outbuilding, such as for garden tools
dismissed or cast off, as a firm does with jobs

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a garden hut and a verb meaning cast off, as firms do with staff.

clue.text: Class for actors, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be heard, spoken out

parts.note: the actors in a play are the cast

explanation.surface: A lesson given for performers, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank or stratum is a class in society.

clue.text: Rabbit's tail trimmed to a point

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
trimmed means cut

explanation.surface: A bunny's tail has been clipped to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, erect tail, like that of a rabbit, hare or deer, has this name.

clue.text: Outstanding seaside feature

parts.note: outstanding means excellent, but here literally standing out into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A platform jutting out from the shore into the water is a classic seaside attraction.

clue.text: Shady character sets up important people

indicators.note: in a down clue sets up means the word is raised, read backwards

parts.note: VIPs are very important persons

explanation.surface: A dodgy type frames some dignitaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets up' turns VIPS around. A SPIV is British slang for a flashy petty crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A smartly dressed small-time dealer in black-market goods is a shady character.

clue.text: Egghead spoke in French with one on the issue

parts.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter
dit is French for said
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intellectual addressed the subject in French alongside a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual; it gives the head letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: One printing of a publication, such as a newspaper or magazine, is an issue.

clue.text: Substitute one fabric with another

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric for upholstery
lace is another fabric

explanation.surface: Swap one material for a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something new in place of another is to substitute, as a verb.

clue.text: Mass meeting, for example

parts.note: a mass meeting suggests a rally, but Mass is the Catholic Eucharist, a kind of worship

explanation.definitionFit: Mass is a form of religious worship gathering, an example of the category.
